payload.claim: The module docstring (line 23) promises the mutant is put back "on every path out", and `_judge_one`'s own comment (lines 84-87) treats an unrestored tree as the single most severe outcome it must catch — but the restore is wrapped in `except MutationError as exc:` only. `restore_mutant` (saffron/mutation.py) calls `target.read_bytes()` and `target.write_bytes()` outside any try/except of its own, so a filesystem failure during restore (permissions, a deleted/moved file, disk full) raises a bare `OSError` that escapes this narrow catch, propagates out of `witness_gate` uncaught, and skips the `error`-status reporting this gate exists to guarantee for every other failure mode. No test in tests/test_witness_gate.py exercises a restore failure of any kind, so this gap is invisible to the suite and only shows up when a real I/O error occurs during a real repo's test run — exactly the boundary the gate's own docstring says it is closing.
